metrics.rationale: User requires '可见光波段 450-650 nm 尽可能高的反射率（用于 RGB 通道成像）' - high reflectance in visible band for RGB imaging.
User requires '近红外波段 700-1000 nm 尽可能高的透过率（用于 NIR 通道）' - high transmittance in NIR band for NIR imaging.

standard.metric_rationale: These two metrics directly capture the dual-band dichroic requirement: maximize reflectance in 450-650 nm (visible/RGB) and maximize transmittance in 700-1000 nm (NIR). Together they inherently minimize crosstalk - high reflectance in visible means low transmittance there, and high transmittance in NIR means low reflectance there. I deliberately omit worst_case variants because the user said '尽可能高' (as high as possible) without specifying uniformity across the band, and mean values better reflect overall imaging performance. I omit absorption metrics because dielectric TiO2/SiO2 stacks have negligible absorption, and the user did not mention thermal or loss requirements. The 45° angle is included because the user explicitly stated '45 度入射'. Polarization is omitted because the user did not specify it, and multispectral cameras typically use unpolarized light.
standard.formula_rationale: The user requires high performance in both the visible and NIR bands equally, with no stated priority for one over the other. Adding the two metrics ensures that the score rewards improvements in either band, encouraging designs that achieve high reflectance for RGB imaging and high transmittance for NIR imaging simultaneously. This sum directly addresses the crosstalk reduction goal because maximizing visible reflectance keeps visible light out of the NIR path, while maximizing NIR transmittance keeps NIR light out of the visible path.
